quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We are leaving for Paris tomorrow.'
options: They said they were leaving for Paris the next day.
They said they are leaving for Paris tomorrow.
They said they were leaving for Paris tomorrow.
quests.correctAnswer: They said they were leaving for Paris the next day.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We are leaving for Paris tomorrow.'
quests.hint: 'Are leaving' → 'were leaving' AND 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'. Both must shift.
quests.explanation: Two changes are needed: 'are leaving' → 'were leaving' and 'tomorrow' → 'the next day'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Will you help me with this project?'
options: She asked if I would help her with that project.
She asked if I will help her with this project.
She asked would I help her with that project.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked if I would help her with that project.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Will you help me with this project?'
quests.hint: Multiple shifts: 'will' → 'would', 'you' → 'I', 'me' → 'her', 'this' → 'that'.
quests.explanation: Four shifts occur: 'will' → 'would', 'you' → 'I', 'me' → 'her', 'this' → 'that'. Use 'if' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The sign said, 'Please don't park here.'
options: The sign told drivers not to park there.
The sign told drivers not to park here.
The sign said drivers don't park here.
quests.correctAnswer: The sign told drivers not to park there.
quests.sentence: The sign said, 'Please don't park here.'
quests.hint: Negative polite imperative: 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Here' → 'there'.
quests.explanation: 'Please don't park' is a polite negative instruction → 'told drivers not to park'. 'Here' shifts to 'there'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I have been working here for three years.'
options: She said she had been working there for three years.
She said she has been working there for three years.
She said she had been working here for three years.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she had been working there for three years.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I have been working here for three years.'
quests.hint: Present perfect continuous → past perfect continuous. 'Here' → 'there'.
quests.explanation: 'Have been working' shifts to 'had been working'. 'Here' shifts to 'there'. Both changes are required.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'When did you last see him?'
options: He asked when I had last seen him.
He asked when I last saw him.
He asked when did I last see him.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked when I had last seen him.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'When did you last see him?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: drop 'did', use statement order, shift 'see' to 'had seen'.
quests.explanation: Drop 'did', use statement word order. 'See' shifts to 'had seen' (past perfect). 'You' → 'I'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'You must not use your phone in class.'
options: The teacher told us not to use our phones in class.
The teacher told us must not use our phones in class.
The teacher said must not use phones in class.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher told us not to use our phones in class.
quests.sentence: The teacher said, 'You must not use your phone in class.'
quests.hint: 'Must not' for prohibition → 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. Pronoun shifts.
quests.explanation: 'Must not use' (prohibition) is reported as 'not to use'. 'Your phone' → 'our phones'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'She doesn't speak French, but she is learning.'
options: He said she didn't speak French but she was learning.
He said she doesn't speak French but she is learning.
He said she didn't speak French but she had been learning.
quests.correctAnswer: He said she didn't speak French but she was learning.
quests.sentence: He said, 'She doesn't speak French, but she is learning.'
quests.hint: Both verbs shift: 'doesn't speak' → 'didn't speak' and 'is learning' → 'was learning'.
quests.explanation: Both clauses shift: 'doesn't speak' → 'didn't speak' and 'is learning' → 'was learning'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'How long have you been waiting?'
options: She asked how long I had been waiting.
She asked how long have I been waiting.
She asked how long I have been waiting.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked how long I had been waiting.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'How long have you been waiting?'
quests.hint: Present perfect continuous shifts to past perfect continuous. Statement order used.
quests.explanation: 'Have been waiting' shifts to 'had been waiting'. Use statement word order with 'you' → 'I'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The professor said, 'Hand in your project by Wednesday.'
options: The professor told students to hand in their projects by Wednesday.
The professor said students hand in your projects by Wednesday.
The professor told students hand in their projects by Wednesday.
quests.correctAnswer: The professor told students to hand in their projects by Wednesday.
quests.sentence: The professor said, 'Hand in your project by Wednesday.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + students + to + hand in'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Hand in' is an imperative → 'told students to hand in'. 'Your project' → 'their projects'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I will call you as soon as I arrive.'
options: She said she would call me as soon as she arrived.
She said she will call me as soon as she arrives.
She said she would call me as soon as I arrived.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she would call me as soon as she arrived.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I will call you as soon as I arrive.'
quests.hint: 'Will' → 'would', 'you' → 'me', 'I' → 'she', and 'arrive' → 'arrived'.
quests.explanation: Four shifts: 'will' → 'would', 'you' → 'me', 'I (arrive)' → 'she arrived'. Note: in time clauses, the present shifts to past.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The nurse asked, 'Are you feeling better today?'
options: The nurse asked if I was feeling better that day.
The nurse asked if I am feeling better today.
The nurse asked was I feeling better that day.
quests.correctAnswer: The nurse asked if I was feeling better that day.
quests.sentence: The nurse asked, 'Are you feeling better today?'
quests.hint: 'Are feeling' → 'was feeling', 'today' → 'that day'. Use 'if' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Are feeling' shifts to 'was feeling'. 'Today' shifts to 'that day'. Use 'if' for yes/no questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Dad said, 'Don't leave the house alone.'
options: Dad told her not to leave the house alone.
Dad told her to not leave the house alone.
Dad said her not to leave the house alone.
quests.correctAnswer: Dad told her not to leave the house alone.
quests.sentence: Dad said, 'Don't leave the house alone.'
quests.hint: Negative imperative: 'told + object + not to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: Negative commands use 'told + object + not to + infinitive'. 'Don't leave' → 'not to leave'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: They said, 'We were watching TV when the power went out.'
options: They said they had been watching TV when the power went out.
They said they were watching TV when the power went out.
They said they had been watching TV when the power had gone out.
quests.correctAnswer: They said they had been watching TV when the power went out.
quests.sentence: They said, 'We were watching TV when the power went out.'
quests.hint: Past continuous → past perfect continuous. The second verb ('went out') stays past simple.
quests.explanation: 'Were watching' shifts to 'had been watching'. 'Went out' (past simple) stays as past simple because it marks the interrupting event.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'How much does it cost?'
options: He asked how much it cost.
He asked how much does it cost.
He asked how much it costs.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked how much it cost.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'How much does it cost?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: drop 'does', use statement order, and 'cost' shifts back.
quests.explanation: Drop the auxiliary 'does', use statement word order, and 'cost' shifts back (present simple → past simple).

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The librarian said, 'Return your library books before the end of term.'
options: The librarian told students to return their library books before the end of term.
The librarian said students return your library books before the end of term.
The librarian told students returning their library books before the end of term.
quests.correctAnswer: The librarian told students to return their library books before the end of term.
quests.sentence: The librarian said, 'Return your library books before the end of term.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + students + to + return'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: 'Return' is an imperative → 'told students to return'. 'Your library books' becomes 'their library books'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I may not come to the wedding, as I'm busy.'
options: She said she might not come to the wedding as she was busy.
She said she may not come to the wedding as she is busy.
She said she might not come to the wedding as she is busy.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she might not come to the wedding as she was busy.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I may not come to the wedding, as I'm busy.'
quests.hint: 'May not' → 'might not'. 'I'm busy' → 'she was busy'. Two shifts required.
quests.explanation: 'May' shifts to 'might'. 'Am' (in 'I'm busy') shifts to 'was'. Both changes are needed.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher asked, 'Why haven't you finished the assignment?'
options: The teacher asked why I hadn't finished the assignment.
The teacher asked why haven't I finished the assignment.
The teacher asked why I haven't finished the assignment.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher asked why I hadn't finished the assignment.
quests.sentence: The teacher asked, 'Why haven't you finished the assignment?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: statement order, 'you' → 'I', 'haven't' → 'hadn't'.
quests.explanation: Use statement word order. 'You' → 'I', 'haven't finished' → 'hadn't finished'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The supervisor said, 'Speak politely to all customers.'
options: The supervisor instructed the staff to speak politely to all customers.
The supervisor instructed the staff speaking politely to all customers.
The supervisor said speak politely to all customers.
quests.correctAnswer: The supervisor instructed the staff to speak politely to all customers.
quests.sentence: The supervisor said, 'Speak politely to all customers.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'instructed + staff + to + speak'.
quests.explanation: 'Speak' is an imperative. It is reported as 'instructed the staff to speak politely to all customers'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'She will have graduated by next June.'
options: He said she would have graduated by the following June.
He said she will have graduated by next June.
He said she had graduated by the following June.
quests.correctAnswer: He said she would have graduated by the following June.
quests.sentence: He said, 'She will have graduated by next June.'
quests.hint: Future perfect ('will have graduated') → conditional perfect ('would have graduated'). 'Next' → 'the following'.
quests.explanation: 'Will have graduated' (future perfect) becomes 'would have graduated'. 'Next June' shifts to 'the following June'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She asked, 'Who told you that?'
options: She asked who had told me that.
She asked who told me that.
She asked who tells me that.
quests.correctAnswer: She asked who had told me that.
quests.sentence: She asked, 'Who told you that?'
quests.hint: 'Told' shifts to 'had told'. 'You' shifts to 'me'. Statement order used.
quests.explanation: Past simple 'told' becomes past perfect 'had told' in reported speech. 'You' shifts to 'me'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The teacher said, 'Write neatly and check your spelling.'
options: The teacher reminded students to write neatly and check their spelling.
The teacher reminded students write neatly and check their spelling.
The teacher reminded students to write neatly and to check your spelling.
quests.correctAnswer: The teacher reminded students to write neatly and check their spelling.
quests.sentence: The teacher said, 'Write neatly and check your spelling.'
quests.hint: Double imperative: 'reminded + students + to + write... and check'. 'Your' → 'their'.
quests.explanation: Two imperatives joined by 'and'. Report with 'to + verb' for the first and 'verb' for the second (parallel). 'Your' → 'their'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I used to play the piano when I was younger.'
options: She said she used to play the piano when she was younger.
She said she uses to play the piano when she was younger.
She said she had used to play the piano when she was younger.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she used to play the piano when she was younger.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I used to play the piano when I was younger.'
quests.hint: 'Used to' does not change in reported speech. Pronouns shift.
quests.explanation: 'Used to' is retained unchanged in reported speech. 'I' → 'she', 'I was' → 'she was'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'Is this bus going to the airport?'
options: He asked if that bus was going to the airport.
He asked if this bus is going to the airport.
He asked was that bus going to the airport.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked if that bus was going to the airport.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'Is this bus going to the airport?'
quests.hint: 'Is going' → 'was going', 'this' → 'that'. Use 'if' and statement order.
quests.explanation: 'Is going' → 'was going'. The deictic 'this' → 'that'. Use 'if' for yes/no questions.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: Mum said, 'Take your umbrella - it looks like rain.'
options: Mum told me to take my umbrella as it looked like rain.
Mum told me to take your umbrella as it looks like rain.
Mum said to take my umbrella as it looked like rain.
quests.correctAnswer: Mum told me to take my umbrella as it looked like rain.
quests.sentence: Mum said, 'Take your umbrella - it looks like rain.'
quests.hint: Imperative with reason clause. 'Your' → 'my'. 'Looks' → 'looked'.
quests.explanation: 'Take' is an imperative → 'told me to take'. 'Your' → 'my'. The reason clause verb 'looks' shifts to 'looked'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He said, 'They have been married for twenty years.'
options: He said they had been married for twenty years.
He said they have been married for twenty years.
He said they had been being married for twenty years.
quests.correctAnswer: He said they had been married for twenty years.
quests.sentence: He said, 'They have been married for twenty years.'
quests.hint: Present perfect passive ('have been married') shifts to past perfect passive ('had been married').
quests.explanation: 'Have been married' (present perfect passive) shifts to 'had been married' (past perfect passive).

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'What do you think about the proposal?'
options: He asked what I thought about the proposal.
He asked what do I think about the proposal.
He asked what I think about the proposal.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked what I thought about the proposal.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'What do you think about the proposal?'
quests.hint: Wh-question: drop 'do', use statement order, 'think' → 'thought'.
quests.explanation: Drop 'do', use statement word order, shift 'think' to 'thought', and 'you' to 'I'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The guard said, 'Don't touch the paintings in the gallery.'
options: The guard warned visitors not to touch the paintings in the gallery.
The guard warned visitors to not touching the paintings in the gallery.
The guard said visitors don't touch the paintings in the gallery.
quests.correctAnswer: The guard warned visitors not to touch the paintings in the gallery.
quests.sentence: The guard said, 'Don't touch the paintings in the gallery.'
quests.hint: Negative imperative: 'warned + object + not to + infinitive'.
quests.explanation: 'Don't touch' is a negative command → 'warned visitors not to touch'. The verb 'warned' suits the context.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: She said, 'I ought to call and apologize.'
options: She said she ought to call and apologize.
She said she should call and apologize.
She said she had to call and apologize.
quests.correctAnswer: She said she ought to call and apologize.
quests.sentence: She said, 'I ought to call and apologize.'
quests.hint: 'Ought to' does not change in reported speech. 'I' shifts to 'she'.
quests.explanation: 'Ought to' is retained in reported speech. Only the pronoun 'I' shifts to 'she'.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: He asked, 'Has the package arrived yet?'
options: He asked if the package had arrived yet.
He asked if the package has arrived yet.
He asked had the package arrived yet.
quests.correctAnswer: He asked if the package had arrived yet.
quests.sentence: He asked, 'Has the package arrived yet?'
quests.hint: Yes/No question: 'if', statement order, and 'has arrived' → 'had arrived'.
quests.explanation: 'Has arrived' (present perfect) shifts to 'had arrived' (past perfect). Use 'if' and statement word order.

quests.question: Convert to reported speech: The flight attendant said, 'Pay attention to the safety instructions.'
options: The flight attendant told passengers to pay attention to the safety instructions.
The flight attendant told passengers pay attention to the safety instructions.
The flight attendant said passengers should paying attention to the safety instructions.
quests.correctAnswer: The flight attendant told passengers to pay attention to the safety instructions.
quests.sentence: The flight attendant said, 'Pay attention to the safety instructions.'
quests.hint: Imperative: 'told + passengers + to + pay attention'.
quests.explanation: 'Pay attention' is an imperative → 'told passengers to pay attention to the safety instructions'.
